Or check the logs?

```
trashcan versioner: restore: rename \\?\R:\syncthing-test\folders\test1\.stversions\~syncthing~1.txt.tmp \\?\R:\syncthing-test\folders\test1\.stversions\1.txt: The system cannot find the file specified.
```

The issue seems to actually be very old.

Are the two issues about the exact same thing, or just similar?

Add various tweaks to the Restore Versions modal in order to make it more usable in general. In the process, upgrade both fancytree and daterangepicker to their newest versions. The important changes in details are as follows. 1. Wrap the table in a container, which is user-resizable, by default occupying as much space as needed within the screen. This prevents the generation of a giant list pushing everything down the screen, and also keeps the filter, date picker, and buttons visible. 2. Apply various usability tweaks, including support for long filenames, ensuring proper functionality on all resolutions, widening the input fields to fit more text, etc. 3. Upgrade the theme to match the rest of the Web GUI, including using the same set of icons. Ensure that everything works correctly in all supported themes. 4. Upgrade fancytree from 2.28.1 to 2.38.0, and daterangepicker from 3.0.0 to 3.1. In the process, remove all pre-defined fancytree themes and create our own in css/assets instead. This is because it takes much less code to write a theme from scratch for our use case than to override the complex pre-defined one. Signed-off-by: Tomasz Wilczyński ## Screenshots Before & After

issue.title: Restoring versions reports an error but actually works

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
### Summary
Restoring deleted file versions via the web UI works but in some cases it wrongly shows an error that it didn't work.

### Steps to reproduce
The wrong error is not shown in all cases and I'm not sure what makes the cases when it is shown special. But if it is happening it is quite simple to reproduce:

1. Select one or more files to restore via the web UI and confirm.
2. An error is shown that renaming didn't work for each file although all of them could be restored¹, e.g.:
    * ![Screenshot_20200105_040758](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10248953/71774591-4cd49980-2f72-11ea-964f-caa15da8897e.png)
    * ![Screenshot_20200105_182640](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10248953/71783576-fb1b2600-2fe8-11ea-9cb4-273a5d0c1b2b.png)

¹With "could be restored" I mean that the files were under `.stversions` before trying to restore them (Syncthing's versioning put them there as expected). After restoring the files they are again under their old location (as expected).

### Expected behavior
The dialog is just closed unless restoring actually didn't work.

### Further information
The full error message (C&P from the web browser to see the full paths) looks like this:

```
Some items could not be restored:
arch/ownstuff-experimental/os/x86_64/mingw-w64-qt5-3d-5.14.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.xz	rename /run/media/devel/repo/.stversions/arch/ownstuff-experimental/os/x86_64/.syncthing.mingw-w64-qt5-3d-5.14.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.xz.tmp /run/media/devel/repo/.stversions/arch/ownstuff-experimental/os/x86_64/mingw-w64-qt5-3d-5.14.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.xz: no such file or directory
```

So apparently there's some intermediate file called `.syncthing.*.tmp` involved. Not sure whether that's supposed to happen or not. In theory it should be possible to rename the file `/run/media/devel/repo/.stversions/arch/ownstuff-experimental/os/x86_64/mingw-w64-qt5-3d-5.14.0-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.xz` directly, right?

The Syncthing log doesn't contain anything related.

### Further UI issues
* One screenshot looks also darkened as if a modal dialog was still open. However, I could reproduce this problem only once and it is likely just some weird bootstrap problem.
* I'd rather not elide the text of such error messages and instead just wrap it or show a scroll bar. Otherwise one has to C&P the message to get the full information which is quite inconvenient.

### Version Information
Syncthing Version: v1.3.2
Environment: Arch Linux using official Go package, x86_64, ext4 file system

body:
I think the problem here is related to the logic behind

https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/blob/30fa462e33f025b46e32d18d4a31b640ed23fd71/lib/versioner/trashcan.go#L66-L91

Basically, the error only shows up if the original file no longer exists. In other words, it occurs only when trying to restore a deleted file. On the other hand, if we try to restore a modification of a file that still exists in its original location, then there are no errors.

I've tried to fix to the culprit myself, but I can't really navigate the code with my limited Go skills. I just hope that this clue may be useful for someone else when trying to work on the issue.

issue.title: gui: Fix error in Restore Versions when path exists as both directory and file (fixes #7068)

labels.name: frozen-due-to-age
labels.description: Issues closed and untouched for a long time, together with being locked for discussion

issue.body:
The current code checks whether the same-named item exists in the tree,
and when it does, it re-uses it when adding new children to it. However,
the code doesn't check whether the existing item is a folder or a file.
It rather assumes that it is always a folder, which is not necessarily
the case.

This commit adds a new check to the code, so that the existing element
is reused only when it is a folder, and ignored otherwise.

Signed-off-by: Tomasz Wilczyński <twilczynski@naver.com>
